## Intuition

Explain the idea in plain language first. Use a concrete example before any symbols.

## The math

Inline math uses single dollar signs: the sample mean is $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$.

Display math uses double dollar signs. Add a label to number and reference it:

$$
\hat{\sigma}^2 = \frac{1}{n-1}\sum_{i=1}^{n}\left(x_i - \bar{x}\right)^2
$$ {#eq-variance}

Refer to it anywhere as @eq-variance.

Multi-line derivations use `aligned`:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbb{E}[\bar{x}] &= \mathbb{E}\Big[\tfrac{1}{n}\textstyle\sum_i x_i\Big] \\
                    &= \tfrac{1}{n}\textstyle\sum_i \mathbb{E}[x_i] \\
                    &= \mu
\end{aligned}
$$

::: {#def-estimator}
## Unbiased estimator
An estimator $\hat{\theta}$ is unbiased if $\mathbb{E}[\hat{\theta}] = \theta$.
:::

## The code

A plain code block (shown, not run) with a copy button:

```python
import numpy as np
x = np.array([2.1, 3.4, 1.9, 4.2])
print(x.mean(), x.var(ddof=1))
```

A block with a file name:

```{.python filename="variance.py"}
def sample_variance(x):
    m = sum(x) / len(x)
    return sum((xi - m) ** 2 for xi in x) / (len(x) - 1)
```

The same idea in several languages, as tabs:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Python
```python
df["value"].var(ddof=1)
```
## R
```r
var(df$value)
```
## SQL
```sql
SELECT VAR_SAMP(value) AS sample_variance FROM measurements;
```
:::

## A figure from live code

This cell runs on your computer when you render, and the chart is saved automatically.

```{python}
#| label: fig-sampling
#| fig-cap: "Sample means cluster around the true mean as n grows."
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
ns = [5, 30, 200]
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 3.4))
for n, c in zip(ns, ["#C7D2FE", "#818CF8", "#4F46E5"]):
    means = rng.normal(0, 1, (4000, n)).mean(axis=1)
    ax.hist(means, bins=60, density=True, alpha=.85, color=c, label=f"n = {n}")
ax.set_xlabel("Sample mean"); ax.set_ylabel("Density")
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
ax.legend(frameon=False)
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
```

See @fig-sampling for the effect of sample size.

## A comparison table

| Estimator | Formula | Unbiased? |
|---|---|---|
| Sample mean | $\bar{x}$ | Yes |
| Variance with $n$ | $\frac{1}{n}\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2$ | No |
| Variance with $n-1$ | $\frac{1}{n-1}\sum (x_i-\bar{x})^2$ | Yes |
